title: Tax Laws Amendment (Fairer Taxation of Excess Concessional Contributions) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would replace the separate tax on excess concessional superannuation contributions with ordinary income tax treatment and allow members to release excess amounts.
Excess contributions would be taxed at the individual’s marginal rate with a 15 per cent offset, and up to 85 per cent could be released.
The changes would apply from the 2013-14 income year alongside a separate bill imposing a charge to account for the timing advantage from excess contributions.
changes: The offset could not be refunded, carried forward or transferred.
Release elections would generally be due within 21 days of the notice and could not be revoked.
Providers could choose whether to release money from defined benefit interests, non-complying funds or interests supporting income streams.
Individuals could object to excess contribution determinations under the tax objection process.
summary.affected: Individuals exceeding their concessional superannuation contribution caps, superannuation providers and the Commissioner of Taxation are affected.

acts.title: Tax Laws Amendment (Fairer Taxation of Excess Concessional Contributions) Act 2013
